title: How Much Should Your Business be Spending on Digital Marketing?

facts.fact: IMPACT's guidance says new or growth-focused companies often spend 10–20% of gross revenue on marketing.
facts.quote: New or growth-focused companies often spend 10–20% of gross revenue on marketing.

facts.fact: IMPACT's guidance says established companies with consistent revenue might spend 5–10% of gross revenue on marketing to maintain momentum.
facts.quote: Established companies with consistent revenue might spend 5–10% of gross revenue on marketing to maintain momentum.

facts.fact: IMPACT states that a small B2B service company might find 7% of revenue sufficient for marketing spend.
facts.quote: A small B2B service company might find 7% sufficient, while a fast-scaling SaaS company may need to lean toward 20%.

facts.fact: IMPACT states that a fast-scaling SaaS company may need to lean toward 20% of revenue on marketing.
facts.quote: a fast-scaling SaaS company may need to lean toward 20%.

facts.fact: IMPACT notes that percentages such as 5%, 10%, and even 20% of revenue are commonly cited for marketing budgets, without clear explanation of what they mean.
facts.quote: There are percentages thrown around (5%, 10%, even 20% of revenue)

facts.fact: The IMPACT article was last updated on October 30, 2025.
IMPACT says it has worked with hundreds of companies on improving their digital marketing using the Endless Customers System.
facts.quote: we’ve worked with hundreds of companies on improving their digital marketing

facts.fact: IMPACT says there are four main areas companies need to spend on for digital marketing.
facts.quote: we’ve found there are four main areas you need to spend on
